statement_summary: Written information security program with an index of its parts
Qualified Individual and HIPAA Security Officer designated in writing; named deputy
Annual written risk assessment and update within 90 days of material change (acquisition, offshore expansion, new AI)
Risk acceptance authority and risk appetite
Annual independent assessment; annual penetration test; vulnerability assessments every six months and after material change
Annual written report to the board; quarterly audit committee summary
Policy and standard hierarchy; annual review
Written, risk-rated, time-limited exceptions; Qualified Individual approval for MFA and encryption exceptions
New technology gate for SaaS, AI tools, AI features, and new data flows, with an IRC 7216 basis
Service provider tiering, contract terms, BAAs, and periodic review
Written IRC 6713 and 7216 notice to contractor individuals before access
Offshore program: consent first, SSN masking, U.S.-hosted desktops
Program and HIPAA records kept at least 6 years
Sanctions for security and confidentiality violations
Unique accounts; shared mailboxes only through delegated access
Role-based least privilege; engagement-team folder access; PHI only for health care teams
MFA for everyone; security keys for administrators, partners, finance, and CAS payroll staff; compliant devices for mail
Mandatory client portal MFA; call-back before client MFA or contact changes; e-signature identity verification
Every SaaS service federated to the identity provider; monthly reconciliation of any local accounts
Automatic disable at termination and seasonal end dates
Prior-role access removed within 5 business days of a transfer
Quarterly access reviews; quarterly review of privileged, export, and bank-change rights
Separate privileged accounts with just-in-time elevation; vaulted service accounts
Break-glass accounts for critical tenants, tested quarterly
Separation of duties for e-file release, refund bank changes, and CAS payments
Remote access with MFA and device check; sign-in outside the United States blocked unless approved
Vendor remote access through the privileged access broker, per-session approval, recorded
Service desk identity verification before password or MFA resets
Written incident response plan with BEC and ransomware runbooks covering 314.4(h)(1)-(7)
Report suspected incidents immediately and within 1 hour
Record discovery, confirmation, and determination dates
Severity 1 activates the crisis management team within 2 hours
Breach and disclosure determinations recorded in the decision log
Meet notification deadlines (IRS next business day, FTC 30 days, states, covered entity clients per BAA)
Freeze refund bank changes and CAS payments during a suspected compromise
No ransom without approvals, OFAC check, and law enforcement report
Annual exercise for each runbook, including one with counsel and executives
Lessons learned within 30 days, fed into P01 and P07
Service provider notices open an incident
Encrypt Restricted data at rest and in transit; no plain attachments
PHI only in the restricted enclave, engagement team access
Inventory of Restricted data locations and recipients, including AI sub-processors
Disclose tax return information only as 301.7216-2 permits or with prior signed consent; consent expiry tracked
No offshore routing before consent; SSNs masked for offshore preparers
Retention schedule and annual disposal run; disposal within two years of last use unless an exception applies
Certified destruction of paper; wipe certificates for drives and leased printers
Immutable encrypted backups; quarterly restore tests
Client data in AI tools only if approved for that class with an IRC 7216 basis
Annual acknowledgment and confidentiality agreement citing 7216 and 6713
Training before access and annually; quarterly phishing simulations plus a January seasonal simulation
Call-back verification for bank, address, email, and payee changes (tax and CAS)
No client data on personal devices or unapproved services; phones enrolled in device management
Returns delivered through the portal or enforced encryption
Approved AI tools only; no client data in public chatbots; human check of AI output
Access client files only as work requires; access logged and reviewed
